q-1418.name: Question 1
q-1418.problem: An adult drinks a cup of coffee that contains $110$ mg of caffeine, and each hour the amount of caffeine in their body decreases by $15%.$ To the nearest integer, how much caffeine will be left in their system after $11$ hours?
q-1418.worked_solution:
The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay rate $r$) is

$$
y=a(1-r)^{t}.
$$

In our case, we have the following:

- $a=110$ is the initial amount of caffeine in the adult's body.

- $r=0.15$ is the decay rate ($15%$ expressed as a decimal).

- $t=$ the time, in hours.

Therefore, the correct expression for $y$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =110\cdot (1-0.15)^{t} \\  & =110\cdot (0.85)^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the expression for $t=11$ hours, we get

$$
y(11)=110\cdot (0.85)^{11}≈18.
$$

Hence, after $11$ hours, there will be $18$ mg of caffeine left in their system.

q-1418.html:
Question 1
?

An adult drinks a cup of coffee that contains 110 mg of caffeine, and each hour the amount of caffeine in their body decreases by 15%. To the nearest integer, how much caffeine will be left in their system after 11 hours?

a
18 mg
b
7 mg
c
9 mg
d
14 mg
e
13 mg
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay rate r) is

y=a(1−r)t.

In our case, we have the following:

  • a=110 is the initial amount of caffeine in the adult's body.

  • r=0.15 is the decay rate (15% expressed as a decimal).

  • t= the time, in hours.

Therefore, the correct expression for y is

y=110⋅(1−0.15)t=110⋅(0.85)t.

Evaluating the expression for t=11 hours, we get

y(11)=110⋅(0.85)11≈18.

Hence, after 11 hours, there will be 18 mg of caffeine left in their system.

q-62052.name: Question 2
q-62052.problem: Austin's average monthly profit has been decreasing at a rate of $6%$ every year. If he initially recorded an average monthly profit of $$58\,000$, then which function correctly represents $p(t),$ Austin's average monthly profit since the start of the decline?
q-62052.worked_solution:
The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay rate $r$) is

$$
p(t)=a(1-r)^{t}.
$$

In our case, we have the following:

- $a=58\,000$ is the initial average monthly profit.

- $r=0.06$ is the decay rate ($6%$ expressed as a decimal).

- $t=$ the time, in years.

Therefore, the correct expression for $p$ is

$$
p(t)=58\,000\cdot (1-0.06)^{t}=58\,000\cdot (0.94)^{t}.
$$

q-62052.html:
Question 2
?

Austin's average monthly profit has been decreasing at a rate of 6% every year. If he initially recorded an average monthly profit of $58000, then which function correctly represents p(t), Austin's average monthly profit since the start of the decline?

a
p(t)=58000⋅(0.94)t
b
p(t)=58000⋅(0.6)t
c
p(t)=58000⋅(0.96)t
d
p(t)=58000⋅(0.06)t
e
p(t)=58000⋅(0.4)t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay rate r) is

p(t)=a(1−r)t.

In our case, we have the following:

  • a=58000 is the initial average monthly profit.

  • r=0.06 is the decay rate (6% expressed as a decimal).

  • t= the time, in years.

Therefore, the correct expression for p is

p(t)=58000⋅(1−0.06)t=58000⋅(0.94)t.

q-62061.name: Question 3
q-62061.problem:
A lake currently has a depth of $320$ feet. The depth of the lake is expected to decrease by one-tenth every year.

The function $d(t)$ models the depth of the lake after $t$ years and is given by

$$
d(t)=320\cdot {(\text{___})}^{t}.
$$

What number is missing?
q-62061.worked_solution:
If the depth reduces by $\frac{1}{10}$ every month, then $\frac{9}{10}$ of the depth remains every year. So the decay factor is $\frac{9}{10}.$

The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay factor $b$) is

$$
d(t)=a{b}^{t}.
$$

In our case, we have the following:

- $a=320$ is the initial depth.

- $b=\frac{9}{10}$ is the decay factor.

- $t=$ the time, in years.

Therefore, the correct expression for $d(t)$ is

$$
d(t)=320\cdot {(\frac{9}{10})}^{t}.
$$

So the missing number is $\frac{9}{10}.$

q-62061.html:
Question 3
?

A lake currently has a depth of 320 feet. The depth of the lake is expected to decrease by one-tenth every year.

The function d(t) models the depth of the lake after t years and is given by

d(t)=320⋅(___)t.

What number is missing?

a
110
b
109
c
10
d
710
e
910
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If the depth reduces by 110 every month, then 910 of the depth remains every year. So the decay factor is 910.

The formula for exponential decay (in terms of a decay factor b) is

d(t)=abt.

In our case, we have the following:

  • a=320 is the initial depth.

  • b=910 is the decay factor.

  • t= the time, in years.

Therefore, the correct expression for d(t) is

d(t)=320⋅(910)t.

So the missing number is 910.
